Let me quickly look at what the project does so the suggestion fits it.

input.description: List repo files and read README

result.output:
# PlanWorldSimulator world generator

Describe a planning benchmark in plain language and generate a playable world from it.
See [docs/design-decisions](docs/design-decisions) for the architecture.

The generator is a fake for now: it walks through the real steps (storyline, copy
template, fill template, tests) and writes a world folder, but does no LLM work.

## Layout

| Path                  | What it is                                                  |
| --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `src/web`             | Website (Vite, React, TypeScript, Tailwind)                 |
| `src/backend`         | API (FastAPI, SQLite via SQLAlchemy and Alembic)            |
| `src/worlds-template` | Base template every world is copied from                    |
| `src/worlds`          | Generated worlds, one folder each (contents are gitignored) |

## Run it

```sh
just up      # build, start in the background, wait until healthy
just down    # stop (database and generated worlds are kept)
```

Open http://localhost:8480 (API docs on http://localhost:8400/docs). If another program uses
those ports, `just up` says so; set `PLANWORLDSIMULATOR_WEB_PORT` and
`PLANWORLDSIMULATOR_API_PORT` in `.env` to change them. Other commands: `just build`, `just logs [service]`,
`just ps`, `just reset` (also deletes the database volume) and `just dev` (live
reload, site on http://localhost:5173). Copy `.env.example` to `.env` to change
defaults.

## Generate real worlds

Put `GEMINI_API_KEY` in `.env`, then `just build` and `just up` as above. The API image
contains the coding agent (OpenCode), the shared world environment and Chromium, so the site
generates real worlds that you can play (about 2–5 minutes each; the first build takes a
while and the image is around 3 GB). Without a key the stack still starts and generates
fake worlds: the API log says which one it uses ("world generation: ...").

Worlds are written to `src/worlds/` on your machine. The model defaults to
`google/gemini-3.5-flash` (`PLANWORLDSIMULATOR_GENERATOR_MODEL` changes it).

Without Docker, on your machine:

```sh
just world-setup                       # once: world environment, Chromium, OpenCode check
just generate "Lemonade" "A lemonade stand ..."   # one world from the command line
just api-local                         # or: the API with the real generator and launcher
just web-local                         # the website on http://localhost:5173
```

A world has three difficulty levels, must pass its tests, and is playable from the website.
See [decision 0008](docs/design-decisions/0008-create-worlds-with-a-sandboxed-coding-agent.md).

## Develop

Needs [pixi](https://pixi.sh), [pnpm](https://pnpm.io) and [just](https://just.systems).

```sh
just install
just format
just lint
just typecheck
just test
```

content.text:
Here's what I'd do. The core idea is that your product has a built-in "wow", and the video should get to it fast.

## The story (one idea)
**"Describe a planning benchmark in a sentence → get a playable, tested world with 3 difficulty levels → an agent (or you) plays it."**

World generation takes 2–5 minutes, so you can't show it live. Pre-record it and cut around the wait.

## 2:00 structure

| Time | Beat | Show |
|---|---|---|
| 0:00–0:15 | **Hook / problem** | One line: planning benchmarks are hand-built and slow to make. Text on screen over the website landing page. |
| 0:15–0:40 | **Prompt → generate** | Type a short description (e.g. "Lemonade stand") into the site and hit generate. Show the pipeline steps ticking by: storyline, template copy, fill, tests. Speed-ramp the wait (about 10× or a cut). |
| 0:40–1:15 | **The world** | Open the generated world and play a few moves by hand. Show the three difficulty levels. Mention it passed its own tests. |
| 1:15–1:40 | **Agent plays it** | Narrator and agent play (your recent commits suggest this exists). Show an agent working through the world. Even a short clip is enough. |
| 1:40–1:55 | **How it works** | One simple diagram: prompt → sandboxed coding agent (OpenCode + Gemini) → world folder → tests → playable. Keep it to 10 seconds. |
| 1:55–2:00 | **Close** | Name, repo, one-line tagline. |

## Practical advice
1. **Pre-generate 2–3 worlds now**, before recording. Use `just up` with a real `GEMINI_API_KEY`. Pick the most visually clear one. Don't depend on a live generation succeeding.
2. **Script the voiceover first** (about 280 words at 140 wpm), then record the screen to match. Do the voice in one clean take, and cut the video to the audio.
3. **Record the screen** with QuickTime or Cmd+Shift+5 at 1080p. Zoom the browser to 125–150% so text is legible. Use a clean browser profile and hide bookmarks.
4. **Show failure handling in one sentence** if you have it, e.g. "worlds must pass their tests or they're rejected". Judges like seeing the rigor.
5. **Edit tool:** For a quick result, use CapCut, iMovie or ScreenFlow. Since this is a repo with Remotion skills available, I can also build title cards, the architecture diagram and captions in Remotion, then render them as overlays.

## What I can do for you
- Write the voiceover script and shot list, timed to 2:00.
- Build the Remotion intro, diagram and captions.
- Check which flow (generate, play, agent) works end to end right now, so you only record what's reliable.

Two things would help me tailor this. What's the hackathon's theme or judging criteria? And is the agent playing a worlds feature you want to headline? Tell me which of the three things above you want first. My default would be the script and shot list.
